parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The equation for reaction 1 is shown.

reaction 1 $$\text{X} \rightarrow 2\text{Y}$$

Reaction 1 is first order with respect to the concentration of X. The half-life of the reaction, $t_{\frac{1}{2}}$, is $900\text{ s}$ at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$.
parts.text: A solution of X with a concentration of $0.180\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ is prepared at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$. Calculate the average rate of reaction 1 over the first $1800\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Complete the rate equation for reaction 1.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Show that the rate constant, $k$, is $7.70 \times 10^{-4}\text{ s}^{-1}$ at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
Calculate the initial rate of reaction 1 when the concentration of X is $0.150\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

Include units.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Catalysts may be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
parts.text: Platinum is a transition element. Explain why transition elements behave as catalysts.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Name the metal catalyst in the Haber process and explain why it is a **heterogeneous** catalyst.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Platinum acts as a heterogeneous catalyst in the removal of nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$, from the exhaust gases of car engines.

Describe the mode of action of a platinum catalyst in this process.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
$\text{NO}_2$ acts as a homogeneous catalyst in the oxidation of atmospheric sulfur dioxide, $\text{SO}_2$.

Write equations for the **two** reactions that occur.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
$\text{SO}_2$ dissolves in water, forming $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$.

$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$ can be oxidised under acidic conditions.

The relevant electrode reaction and its $E^{\ominus}$ value are shown.

$$\text{SO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \quad E^{\ominus} = +0.17\text{ V}$$

Four more half-equations for reactions occurring under acidic conditions, and their $E^{\ominus}$ values, are shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Select the oxidising agent that could oxidise $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$ to $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions under acidic conditions.

Write an equation, and give the $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$ value, for the reaction that occurs.
